A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Entropic Particle Filtering research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms and appendices support comparison despite reformatting, additions and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments, ablations, timing measurements, diversity analyses and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, weaker-reward-model tests, finance and chemistry evaluations, and repeated-run summaries.

M1.justification: Both versions retain Entropic Annealing, ESS-triggered systematic resampling and one-step Look-ahead Modulation. Corrected ESS formulas and trajectory indices reconcile the presentation with definitions and partial-trajectory scoring already described in v1; they do not establish a redesigned algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond v1's mathematical tasks to finance questions from FinanceBench and chemistry problems from NumGLUE, using 128-sample subsets (Appendix G.2, Figure 18). The original mathematical benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons against DORA and REBASE in Figure 15, MCTS and adaptive-branching MCTS in Table 7, and Forest-of-Thoughts in Table 8. These substantially broaden the comparator set while retaining earlier comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce MCTS call budgets of 16/32/64, FoT configurations with 2/4/8 trees, runtime and memory measurements, and a weaker Llama3.1-8B PRM condition. Existing main experimental settings remain stable. Relabeling retained accuracy tables from pass@1 to Top-1 does not establish a changed scoring procedure.

E4.justification: v2 adds calibration comparisons across two PRMs and performance tests under a weaker PRM (Figures 16–17), transfer tests using the mathematical PRM in other domains, and comparative runtime/memory profiling (Table 8). Earlier schedule, backbone, diversity and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 9 newly reports three-run averages with ± quantities for the general mathematical benchmarks, supplementing v1's point estimates. Existing five-run AIME reporting remains. The ± statistic is not defined, and the new run-count disclosure does not establish an increase over v1's runs.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values, but v2 adds results for new comparators, domains, weaker-PRM conditions and three-run summaries. For example, Table 8 reports ePF solving 6/30 problems in 16 minutes versus two-tree FoT solving 7/30 in 76 minutes on eight A100s. These are newly reported comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Algorithm 2 correct ESS from a sum of reciprocal squared weights to the reciprocal of the sum of squared weights. This resolves inconsistency with the correct definition already present in v1 Appendix A.3. The underlying variance analysis is otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: EA and LaM mitigate premature exploitation, improve mathematical reasoning under constrained budgets, and achieve up to 50% relative improvement in task reward. One-step and less-myopic wording clarifies the existing mechanism.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new tests as evidence of applicability beyond mathematics and robustness to weaker PRMs. Appendix E explicitly argues that LaM's benefits exceed reallocating its overhead to more particles, using existing performance curves. The original limitations concerning budgets, overhead and reward-model quality remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents configurations and eight-A100 hardware for new comparisons, plus reward-model and sample details for added tests. Core model paths and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. Conversely, Figure 2a removes v1's disclosure that ground-truth probabilities were estimated using 20 Monte Carlo rollouts.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating related work, v2 substantially expands discussion of SMC planning, reinforcement learning, control as inference and particle impoverishment, including Piché, Macfarlane, Lioutas and de Vries. It also develops explicit positioning against DORA, REBASE and tree-search approaches.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Related Work moves to Appendix A, a contents section is added, pseudocode is rewritten for readability, and many accuracy references change from pass@1 to Top-1. These constitute limited editorial and structural changes rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column layout with extensively rearranged displays and new experimental figures and tables. Figure 2a is redrawn, and Figure 9 is reduced and rearranged while its diversity results remain in the appendix. New Figure 14 redisplays v1 Figure 15 rather than adding results.

improvement.justification: ESS corrections, weaker-PRM tests, broader comparisons and repeated-run summaries improve correctness and empirical support over v1. The gains are qualified by different budget units in the tree-search comparisons, undefined ± quantities in Table 9, and the new claim of consistent superiority conflicting with Figure 17 at N=4. These unresolved issues limit the overall improvement.
